title: Microsoft Teams: Facilitator joins channel meetings
summary: Hold: the automation shown for blocking Facilitator is described as unblocking in Microsoft's reference, so its intended effect cannot be verified. The channel-meeting scheduling guidance also omits Microsoft's warning that disabling meeting policies makes existing meeting join links stop working. The roadmap, licensing prerequisites and most other controls are supported.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked $true provides the automation for blocking Facilitator.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true ... Unblocks Bookings app
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api to null and add this qualification to its note: 'The Update-M365TeamsApp reference labels -IsBlocked $true as unblocking; the blocking value is not reliably documented. Use the Teams admin center Allow or Block action.' Do not substitute $false: that reference also labels a $false example as unblocking.

claims.quote: expand Meetings > Meeting policies and choose the policy ... Under Meeting scheduling ... toggle Channel meeting scheduling to Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowChannelMeetingScheduling $False restricts scheduling for users assigned the policy.
claims.quote: To prevent users with this assigned policy from starting and scheduling channel meetings ... Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowChannelMeetingScheduling $False

claims.claim: The scheduling restriction is described as preventing new meetings while leaving the organiser able to edit existing ones.
claims.quote: After any of the meeting policy settings are turned off ... The meeting join links and conference IDs of all existing meetings of that type that the user previously started or scheduled don't work.
claims.fix: Keep the documented edit-existing-meetings statement, but add to controls[2].note: 'The same page warns that turning off meeting policy settings also disables join links and conference IDs for existing meetings of that type previously organised by the affected user; existing content remains accessible.'
